# Fix: `cmd/fsck --ui=false` exits 0 on a corrupt log, and add the missing regression tests

You are working in a worktree of **`patflynn/tesseract`** — a personal fork of
`transparency-dev/tesseract`. Its `main` was just synced and is identical to upstream
`9e029bc "Update root certificate stores for staging logs (#936)"`.

2. **Do not modify anything under `.github/workflows/`.** The CI story is a separate

3. **Do not touch `~/hack/tesseract` or `~/hack/trillian-tessera`.** Those are read-only
   upstream checkouts elsewhere on this machine. You may read them for reference; leave

4. **Do not add a `replace` directive** for `github.com/transparency-dev/tessera`, and do

5. Keep the diff **small and upstreamable**. This patch is intended to be offered upstream

## The bug

`cmd/fsck/main.go`. Verified by fault injection against a real archived CT log
(solera2019, ~30k entries): a corrupted level-0 tile, a truncated entry bundle, and a
deleted issuer file were **all three detected internally**, and the process **exited 0 in
all three cases**. Two of the three printed no diagnostic at all.

Current code, `main()` at `cmd/fsck/main.go:67-109`:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
...
eg := errgroup.Group{}
eg.Go(func() error {
	defer lsc.Close()
	defer cancel()
	return f.Check(ctx)

})
eg.Go(func() error {
	return lsc.checkIssuersTask(ctx, src.ReadIssuer, *N)
})

if *ui {
	if err := tui.RunApp(ctx, f); err != nil {
		slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "App exited", slog.Any("error", err))
	}
	// User may have exited the UI, cancel the context to signal to everything else.
	cancel()
} else {
	for {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return
		case <-time.After(time.Second):
			slog.DebugContext(ctx, "Ranges", slog.Any("status", f.Status()))
		}
	}
}

if err := eg.Wait(); err != nil {
	slog.ErrorContext(ctx, "FAILED", slog.Any("error", err))
	os.Exit(1)
}

slog.InfoContext(ctx, "OK")
```

Three defects:

**(a) The `--ui=false` path never reaches `eg.Wait()`.** When `f.Check` returns, its
deferred `cancel()` closes `ctx.Done()`. The progress loop hits `case <-ctx.Done(): return`
— a bare `return` out of `main`, not out of the loop. `eg.Wait()`, `os.Exit(1)` and the
final `slog.Info("OK")` are all skipped. The exit status is therefore always 0, and the
"OK" line is dead code in this mode — a *successful* `--ui=false` run never prints `OK`,
which is the tell. The `--ui=true` path is correct: `tui.RunApp` blocks until the TUI
quits, then falls through to `eg.Wait()`.

**(b) LIFO defers cancel the context out from under the issuer check.** Defers run
last-registered-first, so `cancel()` fires *before* `lsc.Close()`. The issuer workers in
`checkIssuersTask` (`main.go:158-171`) can therefore be handed an already-cancelled `ctx`
while they still have buffered fingerprints to look up, producing either a truncated
issuer check or spurious `context canceled` fetch errors. Note that merely swapping the two
defer statements is **not sufficient**: `Close()` only closes the channel: workers may still
be mid-`readIssuer` when `cancel()` runs immediately afterwards. Decide on a fix that
genuinely removes the race — `context.WithoutCancel` for the issuer task is one option, and
signalling check-completion over a dedicated channel so `cancel()` can move below
`eg.Wait()` is another. Pick one, and say in your report why.

**(c) A missing issuer is reported as a warning that does not reach the exit status.**
This is partly upstream: `checkIssuersTask` does return a joined error, but with defect (a)
nothing ever reads it. Confirm that once (a) and (b) are fixed, a missing issuer file
produces a **non-zero exit**. Note in your report — do **not** fix — that
`tessera/fsck/fsck.go` logs `Successfully fsck'd log` from the tree check alone, so that
line is still printed on a run that fails on issuers. That is an upstream-tessera concern
and out of scope here.

## Why this was never caught, and what the tests must therefore do

There is **no test anywhere in this repo that references `fsck`** (`grep -rln fsck
--include='*_test.go' .` returns nothing). Upstream tessera does exercise `fsck.Check()`
end-to-end in four places (`storage/posix/files_test.go`, `storage/aws/aws_test.go`,
`integration/fault/posix/fault_test.go`) but every one of them calls the library function
and inspects the returned `error` directly — which works correctly — and every one asserts
`Check() == nil`. Not one asserts that a corrupt log makes `Check()` fail, and nothing in
either repo executes the `cmd/fsck` **binary**. The defect lives entirely in the ~25 lines
that translate an `error` into a process exit status, and those lines have never been run
by a test.

So the regression test must **execute the built binary and assert on its exit code**.
Testing `f.Check()` in-process would pass on both the broken and fixed code and is
worthless here.

Add `cmd/fsck/main_test.go` covering, all with `--ui=false`:

| Case | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| valid log | exit 0, and `OK` appears in stderr |
| one byte flipped in a level-0 tile under `tile/0/` | exit 1 |
| an entry bundle under `tile/data/` truncated | exit 1 |
| one file deleted from `issuer/` | exit 1 |

The `OK` assertion on the valid case matters as much as the failure cases: it is what
distinguishes "fsck ran and passed" from "fsck returned early having done nothing", and it
is precisely the signal the current code cannot emit.

Build the binary once in `TestMain` with `go build -o <t.TempDir()>/fsck .` and exec it per
case; there is no existing exec-based test in this repo, so establish a clean pattern. Each
corruption case must operate on its **own copy** of the fixture.

Consider also asserting the *shape* of the failure — e.g. that the missing-issuer case fails
for an issuer reason rather than a tree reason — if you can do it without making the test
brittle against upstream tessera's error strings. Use judgement; a brittle assertion is
worse than none.

## Building the fixture log

The test needs a real, signed, static-CT-formatted log on disk: a `checkpoint` signed by a
key you control, `tile/0/…`, `tile/data/…`, and a populated `issuer/`. It must be
**hermetic** — no network, no Docker, no `testdata` fetched at runtime — and the whole
`go test ./cmd/fsck/...` run should finish in well under a minute.

Two viable strategies. Evaluate both, pick one, justify it in the report:

**A. Generate the log in-process at test time (preferred if it comes out clean).** All the
pieces already exist in this repo:

- `internal/ct/handlers_test.go:154-206` (`newPOSIXStorageFunc`) is a working template for a
  POSIX-backed TesseraCT storage stack: `tposix.New` → `tessera.NewAppender` with
  `.WithCTLayout()` and a short `.WithCheckpointInterval` → `storage/posix.NewIssuerStorage`
  → `storage.NewCTStorage`.
- `internal/ct/handlers_test.go:107-138` (`setupTestLog`) shows the surrounding wiring,
  including the trusted-root pool. **Caveat:** it signs with `setupSCTSigner(fakeSignature)`,
  a fake. You need a **real ECDSA P-256 checkpoint signer**, because fsck verifies the
  checkpoint note. See `cmd/tesseract/posix/main.go` (`signerFromFlags`, ~line 365, and the
  `WithCheckpointSigner` call at ~line 281) for how a real key becomes a checkpoint signer,
  and `verifierFromFlags` in `cmd/fsck/main.go:344` for the exact `--origin` /
  `--public_key` (base64 DER) forms the test must pass back in.
- `internal/hammer/chain.go` and `internal/hammer/testdata/` (root + intermediate CA certs
  and keys) are the in-repo way to mint submittable chains. Chains with an intermediate are
  what populate `issuer/`, so make sure at least some entries carry one — otherwise the
  missing-issuer case has nothing to delete.
- `.github/workflows/posix_conformance_ci.yml` is the existing end-to-end recipe (posix
  server + hammer + fsck over `file://`). Read it for the flag combinations that are known
  to work, but do not modify it.

A dozen or two entries is plenty. Do not build a large log.

**B. Check a small pre-generated fixture into `cmd/fsck/testdata/`.** There is precedent
for a checked-in log tree (`internal/client/testdata/log/`). Cheaper and faster, but it
rots when formats change and the origin/public key have to be checked in alongside. If you
go this way, include the generator as a `TestMain`-invoked helper or a documented
`go:generate` so it can be regenerated.

If strategy A turns out to pull in badger antispam or other heavy dependencies you cannot
avoid, say so and fall back to B rather than fighting it.

Note whether the fixture's data tiles land gzipped or plain — it determines whether the
test must pass `--bundle_compressed` (`cmd/fsck/main.go:53`, `client.FileFetcher`).

Then: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./...` across the whole repo — the
